historical_record.description: A two-storey residence was contracted for the corner lot in February 1906, two months before the earthquake, at a stated cost of $4,250 with A. W. Evans as contractor. The corner was addressed 1200 Ashbury until 1909.

A permit of 22 December 1909 replaced or enlarged the corner house as a three-storey building for five families, 28 feet wide, 100 feet deep and 37 feet high, at a stated cost of $8,500, to designs by the architectural firm Rainey and Phillips.
Photographs between 1916 and 1923 show the building considerably expanded, to some twenty-five rooms, and let as the Georgian Apartments.
Four later permits enlarged the building: rooms, baths and stairs in 1920, a garage in 1925, storage rooms in 1928 and a porch in 1930.
A 1948 application to rezone the corner lots from residential to commercial was refused; the change was approved in 1950, and in 1952 the thirteen lots were merged into two.
The apartment building had gone by 1950 — it is absent from that year's fire-insurance maps — and in October 1950 Shell Oil applied for a permit to put a filling station on the site.
A filling station built on the corner in 1953 stayed in service until 1985.
Thirteen condominiums replaced the filling station in 1985, offered at $124,000 to $137,000.

unknowns: The neighborhood newsletter dates the condominiums to 1985; the assessor's roll gives 1986.
